summary: The county’s declared write-in list names Dina Carroll for County Judge. The sample ballot still shows LaFleur and a blank write-in line; the two documents serve different purposes.
content:
## Update — October 2, 2026

Marion County’s official List of Declared Write-In Candidates names Dina Carroll for County Judge in the November 3, 2026 general election. RepWatchr retrieved the county-linked PDF and checked the office-and-name row against the original document.

This closes the desk’s earlier missing-roster gap. The original September 30 article said RepWatchr had not acquired the accepted declaration or qualified-write-in roster. That statement is outdated now that the county’s list has been reviewed. The separate declaration and its filing date have not been acquired.

## Two records, two different purposes

RepWatchr reviewed Marion County’s two-page sample ballot for precincts 1 and 2 on September 29. The County Judge section on page 2 lists Leward J. LaFleur as Republican and provides a blank write-in line. Carroll’s name is not printed in that sample’s County Judge section.

The county’s declared write-in list supplies the candidate name that the blank sample-ballot line does not provide. Read those documents together. The fact that a name is absent from the printed sample is not evidence that the person is absent from the county’s declared write-in list.

## What the documents do not establish

Neither document reports votes or an election outcome. The list does not give Carroll’s declaration filing date or an initial publication date for the county’s PDF. A server modification timestamp is not proof of when a candidate filed.

This review covers the two linked records. It does not establish misconduct, page ownership, a candidate’s private communications, or the terms of any proposed forum.

## Read the original before sharing

Open the county’s declared write-in list and find the County Judge row. Use the November election page to select the sample ballot for your own precinct; the precincts 1 and 2 sample is not a substitute for every precinct’s record.

The original article URL and September 30 publication date are retained. This dated update replaces the missing-roster statement while preserving the September 29 sample-ballot review. AI-assisted reporting, checked against the linked county documents.
